text.p: Here are hightlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet yesterday discussed a plan for Armed Forces reform that would reduce the size of the army to 60,000 by the end of next year, and lower the term of military duty. The cabinet also decided to implement the SOFA agreement, which allowed IFOR force to move across and be stationed in Hungary.
- Welfare Minister Gyorgy Szabo said after Thursday's cabinet meeting that he and Prime Minister Gyula Horn agreed to give themselves two weeks to reconsider his decision to resign.

- The junior coalition partner Free Democrats want Premier Horn to consult them on all major foreign policy and government moves in order to make governmental responsibility acceptable, Free Democrat sources suggest ahead of today's joint meeting of the two parties.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will be among the leaders of 16 Central and Eastern European states meeting in Graz today.
- The Dutch bank ABN Amro will buy Magyar Hitel Bank, the directors of the State Privatisation and Holding Co. decided yesterday.
- Inflation decreased to 1.2 percent in September, bringing the year-on-year figure to 24.8 percent.
- Postabank took up a $75 million loan in London yesterday.
- The pharmaceutical company Richter reported a nine billion forint after-tax profit on revenues of 26.6 billion forints in January-September, said managing director Erik Bogsch.
- Gabor Szeles, president of bus manufacturer Ikarus, said yesterday that the new board of the State Privatisation and Holding Co. supports a strategy worked out to save Ikarus.
- The German vehicle parts manufacturer Knorr Bremse has invested another DM10 million in Hungary.

- More than 1,000 policemen swooped down on main roads leading out of Budapest during the night from Wednesday to Thursday, checking the boots of cars, seeking explosives and weapons. They caught 63 wanted persons and criminals.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- NATO Secretary General Javier Solana confirmed Thursday that an official decision on the expansion of the alliance will be made before the middle of next year and the first new members will be admitted in 1999.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs will host the upcoming series of millecentennial commemorations in Washington on November 12.
- A government decree due to take effect January 1, 1997 stipulates that constant personal protection is to be accorded to five top leaders.

- A working group including two pilots, engineers and other technical staff flew to the U.S. earlier this week to test F-16 and F-18 fighter jets. Testing of French Mirage 2000-5 and Swedish Gripen fighters will follow.

- The German economic daily Handelsblatt said Thursday that National Bank President Gyorgy Suranyi has not won any friends in the western banking community by handing over Vice President Frigyes Harshegyi as a victim to politicians.
- Graboplast announced yesterday that pre-tax profits through the first three quarters were 1.05 billion forints.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The January-September business figures announced by Inter-Europa Bank yesterday exceeded expectations with pre-tax profits of 1.55 billion forints.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Budapest's latest mammoth shopping facility, called Polus Center, a mixture of stores, cinemas, ice rinks and amusement park, is due to open this afternoon in District XV.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
